title: Prompting guide: working without negative prompts
key_findings: States "FLUX models don't support negative prompts".
Naming an excluded thing can pull the model toward it.
Recommends describing the positive visual opposite (e.g. 'a street with no cars' -> 'a quiet pedestrian walkway with cobblestones').
practical_applications: Rewrite every 'no X' in FLUX prompts as what is there instead (plain unmarked paper, empty sky, hands in pockets).
limitations: Vendor guidance, no controlled study; applies to FLUX in general, version not specified.

title: Photographic looks, camera and lens language, art styles, lighting, target colors, and text in FLUX images
key_findings: Recommends naming a style AND describing its visual traits; concrete descriptions beat vague labels such as 'aesthetic'.
Mood/style line at the end of the prompt (documented for FLUX.2 klein); multi-image style reference exists only in FLUX 3 Image.
Text in images: quote exact strings, describe placement and type, proofread output.
practical_applications: For FLUX.1 schnell: write style as traits (line weight, fill, shading, paper) rather than relying on a label alone.
limitations: Written mainly for FLUX 3 / FLUX.2; transfer to FLUX.1 schnell is an assumption to test (ai_tests T1/T2).
Says nothing about artist names.

title: FLUX.1 [schnell] model card
key_findings: 12B rectified-flow transformer, trained with latent adversarial diffusion distillation, 1-4 steps; Diffusers example uses guidance_scale=0.0.
Apache-2.0: personal, scientific and commercial use.
Listed limitations: may not match prompt; prompt following depends heavily on prompting style; may amplify biases.
practical_applications: Keeps our setup legal for shop/client work; explains why steps stay at 4 and guidance is not a knob.
limitations: Card gives almost no prompting guidance.

title: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
key_findings: Guidance can be obtained without a classifier by jointly training conditional and unconditional models and combining their score estimates.
The combination trades sample quality against diversity.
practical_applications: Mechanism behind negative prompts: the negative text takes the place of the unconditional branch; at guidance weight 1 the combination reduces to the conditional prediction alone, so the negative has no effect (our derivation from the CFG formula, see AI_CARTOON_GENERATION.md section 2).
limitations: Abstract only read; the cfg=1 consequence is derived from the standard CFG formula, not stated in the abstract.

title: Fast High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Adversarial Diffusion Distillation
authors: Axel Sauer, Frederic Boesel, Tim Dockhorn, Andreas Blattmann, Patrick Esser, Robin Rombach
key_findings: Distilled student matches teacher quality with 'four unguided sampling steps'; teacher data generated at a constant CFG.
Trade-off: quality kept 'at the expense of prompt alignment'; common issues 'object duplication and merging'.
No adjustable guidance strengths in the student; in editing it sometimes adheres too closely to the input.
practical_applications: Explains schnell-type behaviour (no CFG knob, occasional duplicated limbs/characters, weaker prompt binding): keep scenes simple, one action per character.
limitations: Paper is about SD3-Turbo; the FLUX schnell card names the same method family but BFL has published no schnell-specific results.

title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
authors: Hu Ye, Jun Zhang, Sibo Liu, Xiao Han, Wei Yang
key_findings: ~22M-parameter adapter with decoupled cross-attention for image features; base model frozen.
Image and text prompts can be combined; reusable on models fine-tuned from the same base.
practical_applications: Image-as-prompt is the standard way to carry a character/style reference without training.
limitations: Abstract only; original work is on Stable Diffusion, not FLUX.

title: flux-ip-adapter model card
key_findings: IP-Adapter for FLUX.1-dev, trained at 512 and 1024 px; beta, 'may take more attempts'.
Weights under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License; ComfyUI via x-flux-comfyui nodes; suggests true_gs=2 if results are poor.
practical_applications: Shows the FLUX IP-Adapter route exists but is dev-based and non-commercial -> not for client/shop output without a licence.
limitations: Behaviour with schnell not documented.

title: FLUX.1 Redux [dev] model card
key_findings: Adapter for image variations and restyling; described as working with FLUX.1 base models.
Falls under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License.
practical_applications: Image-variation route for a character master, but the licence blocks commercial use without a BFL licence.
limitations: Card does not discuss schnell explicitly.

title: ComfyUI Examples: Flux
key_findings: Schnell is 'a distilled 4 step model'.
Redux needs sigclip_vision_patch14_384 in clip_vision and flux1-redux-dev in style_models; it 'can be used to prompt flux dev or flux schnell'.
Fill (inpaint/outpaint), Canny and Depth models are dev-based.
practical_applications: Technically Redux runs with our schnell workflow after downloading two files; the licence, not VRAM, is the blocker.
limitations: No VRAM figures; an example page, not a spec.

title: PuLID: Pure and Lightning ID Customization via Contrastive Alignment
authors: Zinan Guo, Yanze Wu, Zhuowei Chen, Lang Chen, Peng Zhang, Qian He
key_findings: Tuning-free identity insertion with a Lightning T2I branch, contrastive alignment loss and ID loss (NeurIPS 2024).
Claims high ID fidelity while keeping background, lighting, composition and style close to the no-ID image.
practical_applications: Face-identity tool for real people; little use for faceless pencil characters.
limitations: Abstract only; the ID loss relies on face recognition, so faceless/cartoon characters are outside its design (our inference, untested).

title: PuLID GitHub repository (PuLID-FLUX)
key_findings: PuLID-FLUX 'can run on a 16GB graphic card'; local gradio demo 'supports 12GB'; fp8 install notes reference flux-dev-fp8.
Code Apache-2.0; ComfyUI implementations are third-party.
practical_applications: Below the documented 12 GB minimum on a 6 GB RTX 3050 -> not feasible now.
limitations: Requirements stated by the authors, not independently tested.

title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation
authors: Nataniel Ruiz, Yuanzhen Li, Varun Jampani, Yael Pritch, Michael Rubinstein, Kfir Aberman
key_findings: 3-5 subject images typical; 4 gave the best DINO/CLIP-T in their test.

Metrics: CLIP-I and DINO (subject fidelity), CLIP-T (prompt fidelity); DINO preferred because CLIP-I cannot separate subjects with similar descriptions; DINO correlates 0.32 vs CLIP-I 0.27 with human preference.
Failure modes: context-appearance entanglement (colour shifts with the prompt), overfitting to the training context, hallucinated details.
practical_applications: Defines how to score character consistency (DINO similarity to the master) and warns that even a trained character drifts with context.
limitations: Correlations with humans are modest (0.27-0.32); results on Imagen/SD with A100/TPU hardware.

title: FluxGym (FLUX LoRA trainer)
key_findings: 'LOW VRAM (12GB/16GB/20GB) support' via Kohya sd-scripts.
Supports Flux1-dev; schnell listed but the author 'Couldn't get high quality results, so not really recommended'.
practical_applications: Local LoRA training on 6 GB is below the documented minimum -> not feasible locally; a dev-trained LoRA would also carry the dev licence question.
limitations: Practitioner tool README; no benchmarks.

title: ComfyUI-GGUF README
key_findings: GGUF loaders for ComfyUI; transformer/DiT models like Flux are less affected by quantization, enabling low-bit quants on low-end GPUs.
LoRA loading is 'experimental' and should work with the built-in LoRA loader nodes.
practical_applications: Explains why FLUX runs on our 6 GB card and that applying (not training) a LoRA is possible but experimental.
limitations: Work in progress; no quality numbers.

title: DreamSim: Learning New Dimensions of Human Visual Similarity using Synthetic Data
authors: Stephanie Fu, Netanel Tamir, Shobhita Sundaram, Lucy Chai, Richard Zhang, Tali Dekel, Phillip Isola
key_findings: NIGHTS: 20,019 human 2AFC triplets.
Agreement with humans: PSNR 57.1%, SSIM 57.3%, LPIPS 70.7%, CLIP B/32 83.1%, DINO B/16 90.1%, DreamSim 96.2%.
DreamSim focuses on foreground objects and semantic content, also sensitive to colour and layout; LPIPS/DISTS dominated by low-level cues like background colour.
practical_applications: Best available automatic proxy for 'do these two character images look like the same thing'; pixel metrics (PSNR/SSIM) are near chance for this.
limitations: Benchmark images come from Stable Diffusion (mostly photo-like); agreement on line-art cartoons is untested; layout sensitivity can reward near-identical poses.

title: Training-Free Consistent Text-to-Image Generation (ConsiStory)
authors: Yoad Tewel, Omri Kaduri, Rinon Gal, Yoni Kasten, Lior Wolf, Gal Chechik, Yuval Atzmon
key_findings: Shared subject-driven attention across a batch keeps a subject consistent without training (SDXL; SIGGRAPH 2024 / TOG).
Consistency measured with DreamSim on background-removed images (notes it can favour slight layout changes); text alignment with CLIP score; 2AFC user study with 3,000 responses.
Limits: appearance and style entangled (works best with one shared style); reduced layout diversity; localisation fails on unusual styles (<5%, fixed by re-seeding).
practical_applications: Evaluation recipe: mask the background, compute pairwise DreamSim within a character set, plus a prompt-alignment score; keep one style per series.
limitations: SDXL-only implementation; not available for our FLUX GGUF setup.

title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability
key_findings: 'Copyright does not extend to purely AI-generated material, or material where there is insufficient human control over the expressive elements.'
'prompts do not alone provide sufficient control.'

Human authors keep copyright in their own work perceptible in outputs and in creative selection, coordination, arrangement or modification; an illustrator inputting their own drawing may have a 'greater claim to authorship'. Cites the Zarya of the Dawn comic decision (human text and arrangement registered, AI images not).
practical_applications: Hand-drawn layouts used as img2img input, human-written text in the HTML layer and documented selection/edits are what make a cartoon post protectable.
limitations: US law only; Thai law not covered; case-by-case.

title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training (Pre-publication)
key_findings: Style is not protected by copyright as such, but there 'may be cases where the replication of style does capture protectible elements'.

Treats stylistic imitation as a possible market harm ('market dilution') in fair-use analysis; cites 'in the style of' prompts naming artists and the flood of images imitating a Japanese animation studio's look.
Notes some AI systems are instructed not to create images in the style of living artists.
practical_applications: House rule: never name living artists, studios or franchises in prompts; describe generic traits of historical movements instead.
limitations: Pre-publication version; US fair-use analysis; not a court ruling.

title: Qualitative Failures of Image Generation Models and Their Application in Detecting Deepfakes
key_findings: Five failure categories: body parts (hands/fingers, eyes, teeth, eyeglasses...), geometry (straight lines, perspective, symmetry), physics (shadows, reflections, support), semantics/logic (spatial reasoning, repeated objects/faces), text/noise/details (garbled text, fine details, crowds).
practical_applications: QC checklist for every AI cartoon panel before publishing.
limitations: Qualitative review drawn from papers and social media; models of 2022-23.

title: เบื้องหลัง 'ขายหัวเราะ ฉบับ AI'
key_findings: Khai Hua Rao AI edition (Apr 2023), presented as the first Thai gag comic made with AI: AI wrote gags and drew images; a 5-6 person team prompted, selected, filled gaps and edited.
The team's own conclusion: AI cannot yet replace human creativity but can convey some humour.
practical_applications: Thai industry precedent: AI as draft generator, humans curate and edit - the same split as our pipeline.
limitations: News feature, publisher self-report; no audience data.

title: The Wild Classics Of Rubber Hose Animation That Inspired 'The Cuphead Show!'
key_findings: Rubber hose: bouncy elasticity, floppy limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, two-button pants; Bill Nolan credited with the approach (Felix, Krazy Kat).
Fleischer the 'rubber hose capital'; Disney moved away in the mid-1930s toward believable movement; out of favour by the mid-1930s; revived by Cuphead.
practical_applications: Trait list for prompting a rubber-hose look without naming characters or studios.
limitations: Trade journalism, not peer-reviewed.

title: How Disney's Snow White became the first full-length animated feature (History.com)
key_findings: Premiere 21 Dec 1937; about 3 years, $1.4M, 750 artists; aimed to compete with live-action features.
Multiplane camera first tested in The Old Mill (1937) to create depth.
practical_applications: Anchor for the 'golden-age full animation' entry: naturalistic movement, depth, painted backgrounds.
limitations: Popular history; the 'first full-length animated feature' claim ignores earlier non-US features (contested).

title: United Productions of America (Nick and Stephen Bosustow Film Collection exhibit)
authors: Indiana University Libraries Moving Image Archive
key_findings: UPA founded 1943; modernism of simplified shapes, flat bold colour without shading, emphasis on the 2D picture plane.
Limited animation: about 12/8/6 drawings per second vs 24, redraw only moving parts, reuse movements; Gerald McBoing-Boing Oscar 1950.
Cites Bashara (Cartoon Vision): by the mid-1950s 'UPA style had become cartoon style'.
practical_applications: Basis for the 'mid-century flat / limited animation' style entry and for limited-animation tricks in our HTML rig.
limitations: Archive exhibit text summarising a scholarly book; Bashara not read directly.

title: The Flintstones Popularizes Prime-Time Cartoons (EBSCO Research Starters)
key_findings: Hanna-Barbera cut costs with stationary backgrounds and about six facial movements; drawings for a half hour reduced by nearly 97% in some cases.
The Flintstones premiered 30 Sep 1960 on ABC as the first prime-time cartoon.
practical_applications: Model for TV limited animation: held poses, mouth swaps, repeating backgrounds - what rig.js puppets do cheaply.
limitations: Reference summary; drawing-count figures differ across sources.

title: Manga, Media and Content in Postwar Japan (nippon.com)
key_findings: Astro Boy premiered 1 Jan 1963 on Fuji TV as Japan's first long-form TV anime; used fewer frames, reused drawings, moved only the mouth in some scenes.
Strong story-manga source material compensated for limited animation and set the manga-to-anime model.
practical_applications: Anime lineage = story strength + economical motion; supports strong scripts with limited rig animation.
limitations: Journalistic history article.

title: Hergé & The Clear Line
key_findings: 'Klare Lijn' label used in Joost Swarte's 1977 booklet; roots in Hergé's Tintin; Brussels School; later Dutch, French, Spanish and Italian followers.
Hergé stressed clarity of drawing, composition and narrative and disliked a style-only reading.
practical_applications: Ligne claire entry: clarity and readability first - fits simple characters on calm backgrounds.
limitations: Critic's essay (expert, not peer-reviewed); the visual rules (uniform line, flat colour) come from secondary summaries.

title: Snack Culture's Dream of Big-Screen Culture: Korean Webtoons' Transmedia Storytelling
key_findings: Webtoon portals from 2003 (Daum) and 2004 (Naver); smartphone era from 2009.
Web-focused attributes: vertical layout, colour drawing, fast production and consumption ('snack culture').
practical_applications: Vertical-scroll grammar for 9:16 story clips and carousels.
limitations: Korea-specific; 2019.

title: ปัจจัยที่ส่งผลต่อศักยภาพภาพยนตร์แอนิเมชันไทยร่วมสมัย (Potential Factors Effecting Contemporary Animated Thai Films)
authors: เขมพัทธ์ พัชรวิชญ์
key_findings: 12 Thai theatrical animated features 1979-2016: classical era = Sudsakorn (2522/1979); contemporary era from 2545/2002 (Pang Pond, Khan Kluay 2549/2006 in 3D, Yak 2555/2012 ...).
Payut Ngaokrachang made Sudsakorn on cels with a 16 mm camera, budget 5M baht; then a gap of more than 20 years; SIPA policy revived the industry.
Only Khan Kluay and Yak succeeded commercially; problems: narrow target audience, TV-to-cinema shift without quality, adapting Thai literature without fresh ideas, technical lag.
practical_applications: Thai audiences reward familiar Thai material told freshly; adaptation alone is not enough.
limitations: KMITL architecture journal; interviews with 4 directors; features only, no TV/web.

title: อัตลักษณ์ทางศิลปกรรมไทยในผลงานภาพยนตร์การ์ตูนของ อาจารย์ปยุต เงากระจ่าง ตั้งแต่ปี พ.ศ. 2498
authors: วิสิฐ จันมา (Vizit Junma)
key_findings: Payut's first Thai cartoon film 'เหตุมหัศจรรย์ในเช้าวันหนึ่ง' 2498/1955; หนุมานเผชิญภัย 2500/1957; Sudsakorn the first Thai feature.

Thai identity via simplified Thai physiognomy and dress, Thai settings and lai thai ornament; Hanuman characters adapted from traditional Thai mural painting with rounded soft forms; rubbery exaggeration in early work.
practical_applications: How to make a cartoon read as Thai without cliché: everyday Thai settings, dress and body types, ornament as accent.
limitations: Naresuan University journal; publication year not visible in the extracted text.

title: วิวัฒนาการทางวัฒนธรรมของการ์ตูนไทยสู่จินตนาการอันก้าวไกลในโลกดิจิทัล (Cultural evolution of Thai cartoons to the far-reaching imagination in the digital world)
authors: ณปภัช อโรชาสิริ (Napapat Arochasiri)
key_findings: Khrua In Khong called the first Thai cartoonist; first political cartoonist Khun Patiphak Pimlikit (Pleng Tripin) under Rama VI.

After 1932: Sawat Chutharop's serialised Sang Thong and comic sidekick Khun Muen (Popeye/Mickey influence); Prayoon Chanyawongse ('king of Thai cartoons', Magsaysay award); children's magazine Tukata (Pimon Kalasee, characters from 1952); Khai Hua Rao three-panel gags (Arwat); post-1967 TV-influenced superhero comics (Asawin Saifah); Chai Rachawat political strip after 14 Oct 1973.
Today: digital tools and manga influence; concern that a distinct Thai cartoon style may be lost; Wisut Ponnimit (hesheit) as a rough-line, idea-first Thai artist known abroad.
practical_applications: Thai lineage for style proposals: Thai gag strip, Thai political caricature line, Thai fable/jakkrawong comics.
limitations: Descriptive review relying partly on web sources; some dates not given.
